original.prompt: Consider the following statements about the additional duty imposed by the United States on imports in July 2026 over forced-labour enforcement:
items: The duty followed an investigation under Section 301 of the US Trade Act, 1974.
India was placed in the 12.5% tier because it had not prohibited forced-labour imports.
Generic pharmaceuticals and smartphones from India fall outside the new duty.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: India was placed in the 10% tier, not the 12.5% tier, because it had notified a ban on forced-labour imports before the duty took effect. Roughly 45% of India's exports to the US, including generic pharmaceuticals and smartphones, are outside the new duty.
original.source: The United States Trade Representative (USTR) investigated 60 economies under Section 301 of the US Trade Act, 1974, over failures to block imports made with forced labour.

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about the additional duty imposed by the United States on imports in July 2026 over forced-labour enforcement:
items: The duty followed an investigation under Section 301 of the US Trade Act, 1974.
India was placed in the 10% tier after its Directorate General of Foreign Trade notified a prohibition on forced-labour imports.
Generic pharmaceuticals and smartphones from India fall outside the new duty.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: All three statements are correct: USTR acted under Section 301, India got the 10% tier after the DGFT notified a forced-labour import prohibition on 13 July 2026, and generic pharmaceuticals and smartphones are among the roughly 45% of India's US exports outside the duty. USTR set 10% for economies that prohibit forced-labour imports and 12.5% for those that do not.
rewritten.source: India's Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) notified such a prohibition on July 13, four days after the hearings closed.
